params.status_of_the_original: The registered procedure was run once on 2001-2021 data and its rule returned 'consistent'. That verdict is NOT acted on and the out-of-sample window was NOT opened. The numbers are recorded below so the amendment cannot be read as a way to get a different answer quietly.

what_the_original_run_showed.selected: trend 250, integral 120, kp 0.1, ki 0.1, kd 0.0, base 0.5
what_the_original_run_showed.in_sample_grid: 530 of 768 eligible; 18% of eligible with positive alpha; median -0.7%; best +1.4% (t 1.26)

params.the_defect: Timing alpha was registered as mean((w_t - wbar) * r_t) * 252 with wbar the strategy's average weight over the window being scored. wbar is not known until the window is over, and for a rule that sells strength it is negatively correlated with the window's own return: in a window where the fund rose, the rule's average weight was low, so the comparison portfolio is handed a small position exactly when a large one would have paid. Under no predictability at all, E[alpha] = -Cov(wbar, window return) > 0 for a contrarian rule and < 0 for its mirror. This is the finite-sample bias of a predictive regression on a persistent regressor whose innovations are negatively correlated with returns (Stambaugh 1999), arrived at through the benchmark. It grows as the window shrinks, so the twelve one-year walk-forward windows carry the most of it and the twelve-year in-sample window the least.
evidence_already_in_the_report: The whole grid's median alpha is positive in 10 of the 12 single test years (up to +10.9% in 2020) while its median over the full twelve in-sample years is -0.7%. A quantity that is positive for nearly every configuration every year, yet negative for most of them over the same years taken together, is measuring the window length.
2013: the walk-forward pick returned +3.7% against +41.6% for the fund and was scored +1.4% alpha, because its average weight that year was about 5% and the comparison was a 5% position.
The mirror is scored with the same bias in the opposite direction, so 'the mirror did worse' was not independent evidence about direction.
params.why_not_just_swap_the_metric: Selecting a new metric after seeing these numbers is a degree of freedom, and the obvious replacements (in-window regression alpha, in-window average weight in any form) carry the same look-ahead. The registered statistics are kept exactly as they are. What changes is what they are compared with: instead of zero, their own distribution on price histories in which no rule can have timing skill. A bias that exists under the null is in that distribution too and cancels.

placebo_nulls.sign_flip (deciding): Each day's (overnight, intraday) log-return pair is demeaned, multiplied by one random sign per day, and re-meaned. The size of every day's move stays on its own date, so volatility clustering and the 2008 and 2020 volatility episodes are preserved; the serial dependence of direction, which is the only thing a timing rule can use, is destroyed.
placebo_nulls.shuffle (reported): The same pairs in random order. Destroys volatility clustering as well; reported to show the result does not hinge on which null is used.
placebo_nulls.construction: 200 histories per null, numpy default_rng seeds 0..199 (sign_flip) and 1000..1199 (shuffle). Built only from 2001-07-13..2021-12-31 returns, on the real dates, first close 1000 and initial cash 1e9 so whole-share and cent rounding cannot differ from the real run in any way that matters. Each history goes through the identical end-to-end procedure: same grid, same eligibility, same selection score, same walk-forward windows.

statistics_compared.S_val: validation alpha of the in-sample pick (real: +4.5%)
statistics_compared.p_value: (1 + count of placebo histories with statistic >= real) / (N + 1); a placebo history with no eligible pick counts as not exceeding

decision_rule.consistent: Under the sign-flip null: p(S_wf) < 0.05 AND the real S_val is above the placebo median of S_val. Only then is the out-of-sample window opened, once, for the configuration already selected.
decision_rule.rejected: Otherwise. The original 'consistent' is recorded as an artefact of the benchmark, the strategy is not adopted, and the out-of-sample window stays unopened.
decision_rule.why_these_thresholds: The walk-forward statistic covers twelve test years including the three validation years, so it is the powered one and carries the conventional 5% one-sided test. Validation alone is three years; asking it for significance would be asking for a number it cannot produce, so it is only required not to be worse than what no skill typically yields.

params.power_stated_in_advance: With twelve test years the placebo spread of S_wf will be on the order of a few percent a year. An edge of about one percent a year, if it exists, cannot be told from none by this test. A rejection therefore means 'no edge large enough to see in twenty years of this fund', not 'no edge'.
reported_but_not_deciding: Share of placebo histories on which the ORIGINAL four-key rule returns 'consistent': the false-positive rate of the rule as first registered.
Placebo mean of S_wf and S_val: the size of the bias in each.

Sharpe of the pick minus Sharpe of the fund, in sample and in validation. A fixed position of any size has the fund's Sharpe when cash earns nothing, so this compares against a benchmark fixed in advance and involves no in-window average. Already visible for the pick (0.44 vs 0.46, 1.33 vs 1.39) and stated here so it is not presented later as a discovery.
closed_degrees_of_freedom: Grid, fixed values, eligibility, selection score, windows and the selected configuration are unchanged from the original registration.
N, both seed ranges and the construction of both nulls are fixed above.
The deciding null is sign-flip. If the two nulls disagree, sign-flip decides and the disagreement is reported.
No second selection is made on the real data.
params.disclosure: This amendment is written after seeing the original run, including validation. It can only make the bar higher: it adds a requirement and removes none that was passed on unbiased grounds.
